newsitem.title: INDIA: More jolts seen for troubled Indian stocks.
newsitem.headline: More jolts seen for troubled Indian stocks.

text.p: Battered Indian stocks are likely to take a further pounding this week as nervous investors brace for political and economic setbacks, brokers said on Sunday.
"The outlook is dismal," said Ajay Mehta, a partner at broking firm Manharlal Shantilal.
He said the benchmark 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) market could drop to 2,900 points if it breached the psychological barrier of 3,228.
Last week the index shed 92.05 points, or 2.75 percent, closing on Friday at 3,254.73.

"We expect the market to begin the week ahead in the same bearish vein," said Sanjay D'Souza, research head at Nucleus Securities, the investment affliate of broking firm Asit Mehta Investment Intermediates Ltd.
"We expect the market to be in the range of 3,150 to 3,300 points this week," he said.
The most keenly awaited event was a scheduled court appearance on Monday in Delhi by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, summoned in a case of criminal conspiracy to cheat.

Last week Rao, who quit as Congress party leader on September 21, was denied protection against arrest in the case. Court officials said Rao was expected to be arrested on Monday, but that he could immediately make a fresh request for bail.
The two other co-accused in the case are in custody in jail pending trial.

Federal police filed charges against Rao last week in a forgery case. Some analysts believe his legal troubles could undermine his Congress party's crucial support for the minority coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Both Deve Gowda's United Front government and the Congress party have denied any cause for concern.

"The market's headed downside," said R. Balakrishnan, president of Dil Vikas Finance Ltd, a broking firm at the National Stock Exchange. He said the political uncertainty could force foreign funds to re-rate Indian stocks.
Analysts said political instability was compounded by darkening economic prospects.
They believe a general slowdown in the economy has hurt growth of many companies' earnings, and predicted results for the six months to September 30 would reflect the contraction.
"The reporting season will prove in black and white everyone's worst fears," said Bharat Iyer, strategist at UBS Securities, the investment arm of Union Bank of Switzerland.
"I don't see the market recovering in the next three months," he said.
The depressed domestic market was bad news for cash-starved companies, analysts said.
On Friday, state-run refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd said it decided to put off its public equity issue worth 4.12 billion rupees scheduled to open in late October.
"The board of directors of the company...has decided to defer the issue until market sentiments improve and the opportunity for a good retail response is available," the firm said in a statement.
On October 3, the State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest commercial bank, is expected to price its $400 million issue of global depositary receipts.
"We feel the issue will sail through smoothly but as far as the pricing goes, a premium may be difficult," said Skindia Finance in a report released at the weekend.
